corrections.why: The record's coordinates match the 1939 replacement, Fire Tower 67, which the county list marks removed. The original 1929 headquarters tower was moved and still stands at the Aiton Heights site.

corrections.proposed: Minnesota Division of Forestry (erected); Itasca State Park today
corrections.why: 143N-36W-2 reads as a township, range and section location code, not an agency.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was moved into Itasca State Park in 1937; the county survey list says it was moved to its present location in 1939. Both dates are kept as separate events.
The county survey list gives the Aiton Heights tower as 100 feet; the NHLR gives 80 feet. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's gone status and agency field look wrong. The firelookout.org coordinates (47.23909, -95.19615) match Fire Tower 67 (1939 ladder tower, county list), which replaced the 1929 headquarters tower; the headquarters tower became the Aiton Heights tower, which stands and is open in summer. Linking the 1929 article's tower to Aiton Heights is an inference from matching descriptions (100 ft, enclosed stairway, forestry headquarters origin); no source says it outright. Move year conflicts (1937 NHLR vs 1939 county list) and height conflicts (80 ft NHLR vs 100 ft county list). Staffing and fires: nothing found in sources read. The Spurr 1953 Itasca fire history on doczz.net returned only a stub with no text. The county table row for Fire Tower 67 reads 1939, 94 ft, ladder; the story gives no build year for it.
